title: Cap. XI: Socinians, Arminians, Walaeus — Garissoles’s arguments closed before Cap. XII
pass_a_gloss: Concerning the Socinians, since they differ in nothing from the Pelagians, what need is there to speak? As for the Arminians, by God's kindness Placeus shrinks from their errors also. And the most learned Walaeus, who answered Corvinus on behalf of the most distinguished Du Moulin, did not hesitate to deny immediate imputation in express words, as we noted above at page 22, and is not on that account thought to favor the Remonstrant party. And these were Lord Garissoles's arguments.
pass_b_english: As for the Socinians, since they differ not at all from the Pelagians, what more is there to say? As for the Arminians, by God's kindness Placeus shrinks from their errors too. The learned Walaeus, answering Corvinus for the distinguished Du Moulin, did not hesitate to deny immediate imputation in plain words — as we noted above at page 22 — and is not for that reason thought to side with the Remonstrants. And those were Lord Garissoles's arguments.
source_text: De Socinianis, cum nihil differant a Pelagianis, quid opus est dicere? Ad Arminianos autem quod spectat, ab eorum etiam erroribus, Dei beneficio, abhorret Placeus. Qui autem pro Clariss. Molineo Respondit Corvino doctissimus Walaeus, is non dubitavit imputationem immediatam disertis verbis negare, uti a nobis observatum est supra, pag. 22. nec propterea partibus Remonstrantium favere existimatur. Atque haec fuerunt argumenta D. Garissolii.

choices.choice: Socinians collapse into Pelagians for this dispute
